quizzes.stem: Under the 2026-07-28 revision, a tool needs a person's answer halfway through a call. How does the server get it?

options.a: It sends the client its own request on an open stream and waits for the reply
options.b: It pauses the call and holds the connection open until the client answers
options.c: It stores the question in a session, which the client resumes later
options.d: It returns an input-required result, and the client repeats the request with the replies

explanation.d: The page says the server answers with an input-required result, and the client "then retries the original request including the additional requested information".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The previous pattern of server-initiated requests is no longer supported."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the pattern works "without requiring a shared storage layer across server instances or requiring stateful load balancing", which a held connection would need.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the pattern allows "servers to request additional information without maintaining any server-side state", so there is no session to resume.

quizzes.stem: A client receives an opaque string called requestState together with an input-required result. What must it do with that string?

options.a: Send back the exact same value on the retry, without reading it
options.b: Discard it, since only the answers to the questions matter on the retry
options.c: Keep it in a cookie so that other calls running in parallel can reuse it
options.d: Decode it to learn what the server wants, then adjust it before the retry

explanation.a: The page says "Clients MUST NOT inspect, parse, modify, or make any assumptions about its contents", and that the client must echo the exact value on the retry.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Clients MUST NOT inspect, parse, modify, or make any assumptions about its contents."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the client MUST echo back the exact value of that field when retrying the original request", and the retry needs it, since the server keeps nothing else.
explanation.c: Ruled out because both fields "MUST NOT be used for any other request that the client may be sending in parallel".

quizzes.stem: A server must collect a payment card number from a user during a tool call. Which mode of elicitation may it use?

options.a: The form one, since the client validates every field against a schema
options.b: Either one, as long as the client shows the form to the person first
options.c: The out-of-band one, where the person visits a separate web page
options.d: Neither one, since a server may never request data from a person

explanation.c: The page says "Servers MUST NOT use form mode elicitation to request sensitive information", and that such interactions belong in URL mode.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Servers MUST NOT use form mode elicitation to request sensitive information", whatever the schema checks.
explanation.b: Ruled out because URL mode "keeps the data out of band so it never passes through the client or the LLM context", and a form always passes through the client.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Elicitation lets a server ask a person for more information", with URL mode for sensitive data.

quizzes.stem: An MCP server on Streamable HTTP receives a request whose Origin header shows an unrelated site. What does the specification require?

options.a: Accept it, since the Origin header is advisory and only logged
options.b: Answer 403 Forbidden, which blocks DNS rebinding attacks
options.c: Close the stream of the next response so that the sender retries
options.d: Redirect it to the authorization server so that the sender can authenticate

explanation.b: The page says "Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks", and that an invalid one gets 403 Forbidden.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "If the header is present and invalid, the server must answer 403 Forbidden", not a redirect.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Closing the response stream is cancellation", which is how a client cancels a request, and it is not an answer to a bad Origin.

quizzes.stem: An MCP server accepts a credential that was meant for another service and passes it unchanged to a downstream API. What does the specification say?

options.a: Allowed, since the downstream API validates the token on its own
options.b: Allowed when the user has consented to the downstream call
options.c: Required, so that the downstream API sees the original audience
options.d: Forbidden: it takes only tokens that were issued for its own resources

explanation.d: The page says "MCP servers MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "MCP servers MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Token passthrough is explicitly forbidden", with no consent exception.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience".

quizzes.stem: A server issues a workflow identifier in a tool result and later acts on whoever presents it. Which attack does this invite?

options.a: None, because MCP sessions already bind every handle to its caller
options.b: Hijacking, since holding the handle is taken as proof of who is asking
options.c: Scope inflation, since the handle carries more permissions than needed
options.d: Cross-site scripting, since the identifier appears in a result

explanation.b: The page says "MCP servers MUST NOT treat possession of a state handle as authentication."
explanation.a: Ruled out because MCP in this revision "is stateless and has no protocol-level sessions".
explanation.d: Ruled out because state handle hijacking is "an unauthorized party obtains or guesses a handle and uses it to read or change another user's state".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the remedy is that "MCP servers SHOULD bind handles server-side to the authenticated user", which is about ownership and not about permissions.

quizzes.stem: A tool wants a person's confirmation, but the calling client declared only roots. What must the server avoid?

options.a: Returning a normal result that reports the confirmation could not be requested
options.b: Including any elicitation request, since the caller never announced support for it
options.c: Ending the call with an error code, since failing is always forbidden
options.d: Signing the state of the call, since the client may tamper with it

explanation.b: The first page says "Servers MUST NOT send an inputRequests that the client has not declared support for in its capabilities."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the practice's server "completes with an error result that says the client cannot be asked", so a normal result of that kind is allowed.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "servers MUST treat requestState as an attacker-controlled input", so signing it is required, not avoided.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a server that needs a capability the call did not declare "returns a MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError with code -32021", which is an error code.

quizzes.stem: Two requests carry the same requestState and arrive within its lifetime, one from the user it was issued to and one from a different user. How should the server treat them?

options.a: Reject the second, because the signed payload names its intended principal
options.b: Reject both, since a state may be presented only once
options.c: Accept both, because the expiry is the only check the specification requires
options.d: Accept both, because a valid signature proves the state is genuine

explanation.a: The first page says the state should carry "the authenticated principal, rejecting state presented by a different principal".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the server must reject "rejecting state presented by a different principal" even when the signature is valid.
explanation.b: Ruled out because these measures "do not by themselves guarantee single-use", so the same user can present it again within the lifetime.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the server also checks "an identifier of the originating request", and the principal.

quizzes.stem: A load balancer sends consecutive calls of one client to different instances of an MCP server on the 2026-07-28 revision. What does the protocol need so that this works?

options.a: No shared storage, since each call is self-contained
options.b: A sticky connection that keeps one client on the same instance
options.c: A resumable stream that another instance can pick up by its event id
options.d: A session identifier that each instance looks up in a common table

explanation.a: The first page says the pattern works "without requiring a shared storage layer across server instances or requiring stateful load balancing", and the second page that every POST stands alone.
explanation.d: Ruled out because MCP in this revision "is stateless and has no protocol-level sessions".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the pattern works "without requiring a shared storage layer across server instances or requiring stateful load balancing".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Resumable streams through `Last-Event-ID` are not supported."

quizzes.stem: A team plans HTTP-style login for an MCP server that runs as a local child process. What does the specification advise?

options.a: Follow the same flow, since authorization is mandatory for every transport
options.b: Use a query-string token, which stdio clients may append to the command
options.c: Skip that flow and read credentials from the environment instead
options.d: Ask the user for a password through form-mode elicitation on each start

explanation.c: The second page quotes the specification: "Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Access tokens MUST NOT be included in the URI query string".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Servers MUST NOT use form mode elicitation to request sensitive information".
